commits.description: Commits replayed onto the server's history.

grafted.description: The commit on the server's history the branch became.

previous.description: Where the server's branch was before.

reason.description: What kind of refusal it was: `invalid_name`, `target_branch`, `case_conflict`, `invalid_tip`, `not_pushed`, `not_on_snapshot`, `conflict`, `merge_conflict` or `diverged`.

rule.description: For an `updated` branch, what allowed it.

status.description: `created`, `updated`, `unchanged` or `refused`; `unchanged` when the server's branch was at the graft already, or ahead of it.

branches.description: One entry per branch; empty when no branch had commits to check in.

gave_change_ids.description: Commits made with plain Git that were given a change id first (their branches were rewritten with it).

refused.description: Whether any branch was refused (the exit status is then `1`).

CheckinRuleJson.description: Why the server let a check-in move a branch it already had.

oneOf.description: The server's branch is in the new commit's history.
This checkout set the branch last, so it replaces its own work.
A rebase that keeps every commit the server's branch had, by change id.

MergeConflictJson.description: One conflicted path in `--json` output (pull v1 `conflict_details` and merge v2 items).

alternatives.description: Abort/skip commands (not part of the ordered sequence).

autostash.description: Autostash commit kept on `refs/stash` (rebase stopped, or re-applying it conflicted).

commit.description: Local commit the rebase stopped on (`operation` is `rebase`).

next_steps.description: Ordered `grit` commands to finish the paused operation.

refresh.description: In a snapshot checkout, the server snapshot the pull refreshed onto.

server_branch.description: In a snapshot checkout, `grit pull <branch>`: the server's branch as the checkout sees it, and what the local branch did.

PullRefreshJson.description: What `grit pull` refreshed in a checkout.

base.description: The real commit the newest snapshot stands for. With `--dry-run`, where the target is now.

behind.description: Other branches with commits of their own still on an older snapshot.

changes.description: What changed in the checkout's paths between the two snapshots; null when the target didn't move.

dry_run.description: With `--dry-run`: nothing was fetched or changed, and the server made no snapshot.

followed.description: Local branches with no commits of their own that moved to the new snapshot: the one named after the target, and others whose commits all landed in the target.

gave_change_ids.description: Commits made with plain Git on the current branch that were given a change id before the rebase (the branch was rewritten with it).

moved.description: Whether the target had moved since the checkout's last snapshot.

previous_base.description: The real commit the checkout's previous snapshot stood for.

snapshot.description: The newest snapshot commit, now `origin/<target>`. With `--dry-run`, the checkout's snapshot as it is.

upstream_ref.description: The local ref holding the newest snapshot, `refs/remotes/origin/<target>`.

PullServerBranchJson.description: What `grit pull <branch>` did in a checkout: the server's branch as the checkout sees it, and the local branch brought onto it.

commits.description: The server branch's commits the target lacks, all shown to this checkout (cut down to its paths).

gave_change_ids.description: Commits made with plain Git on the branch that were given a change id first (the branch was rewritten with it).

made.description: How many of them were made afresh for this checkout.

name.description: The branch, as the server spells it (which can differ in case from the name given, on a server that ignores case).

own.description: Commits of the local branch replayed onto the server's (its own commits, without copies of the server's).

previous.description: Where the local branch was; null when it was created.

projected.description: What this checkout sees of it, now at `upstream_ref`.

reused.description: How many were commits that were there already: checkout commits on the same snapshots that the server's are grafts of (this checkout's own among them), and what it was shown before.

switched.description: Whether `HEAD` was moved onto the branch to rebase it.

tip.description: Where the server's branch is, on its real history.

upstream_ref.description: The local ref holding the server's branch as this checkout sees it, `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`.

was_on.description: The branch `HEAD` was on before, if any.

RefreshBehindJson.description: A branch still building on an older snapshot after a refresh.

RefreshChangesJson.description: What changed in a checkout's paths between two snapshots, as `git diff --shortstat` counts it.

RefreshFollowedJson.description: A branch a refresh moved along with the snapshot.

from.description: The older snapshot it was at.

to.description: The new snapshot it is at.

checkin.description: The check-in done first, when the branch is here.

commits.description: The branch's commits the merge brought in.

follows.description: The branch this checkout follows, when the server merged into another one (its `HEAD` names a different branch now): the merge is not in this checkout's snapshots, so the branch keeps its commits here.

moved_to.description: The new work branch you are on, when the branch you were on was the one merged: that branch is gone here (it stays on the server).

refresh.description: The refresh done after (as `grit pull` reports it); omitted when it failed (see `refresh_error`).

refresh_error.description: Why refreshing this checkout after the merge (or moving to a new work branch) failed. The merge stands on the server; the exit status is 1.
